ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of directors, shareholders, ultimate beneficial owners, and authorized signatories against the UN Consolidated List, UK Sanctions List, OFAC SDN List, EU Consolidated List, and local GFSC enforcement actions. Enhanced due diligence required for any PEP, family member, or close associate, including verified source-of-wealth and source-of-funds analysis. Adverse media, negative news, and sanctions-triggering screening must be completed pre-onboarding and periodically. All screening records are retained in accordance with the Bermuda/Gibraltar AML/CFT regime (minimum five years).

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Bermuda Registrar of Companies – Companies and Plans Database (eGov Bermuda) and, for an optional Gibraltar external branch, the Gibraltar Companies Registry e-registry via the Gibraltar Financial Services Commission (GFSC)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Company names must be in the Latin alphabet; English is the statutory language. No local script or transliteration requirement for a Bermuda Exempted Company. The name must include 'Limited', 'Ltd.', or an authorized abbreviation and must not conflict with any existing registered name. Terms implying government patronage, royal character, or regulated financial activity are automatically scrutinized.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the proposed name is rejected, the applicant may, within 21 days of the rejection notice, file an administrative appeal with the Registrar of Companies. The appeal must state the legal and factual grounds for review and attach any relevant consent from a licensing authority. If the name is initially accepted but conflicts later, the company must annotate the objection and may apply to the Supreme Court for relief. Name reservations can be extended once for an additional 30 days by filing a renewal request and paying the annual extension fee. Alternatively, a fresh name reservation can be submitted immediately without appeal if the rejection is based on obvious similarity.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office is not permissible as the statutory registered office. The Bermuda Exempted Company must maintain a physical registered office at the premises of a licensed corporate services provider in Bermuda. A virtual office may be used for general correspondence, commercial address, and marketing purposes only. For a Gibraltar branch, a physical registered office address is also required. No employees are required to be physically present in Bermuda for this low-risk micro-SaaS business, but management and control must be exercised in Bermuda in accordance with the economic substance rules.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: 15% (moderate-to-low; based on the Low_Risk_Standard tier and the absence of a statutory license for ISIC 6201 software operations; unannounced visits can be triggered by the Registry or AML supervisory bodies only upon reasonable suspicion)

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Companies Act 2014 (Gibraltar), Part II, ss. 5-20 (Incorporation and Registration); s. 44 (Articles of Association); s. 183 (Registered Office)
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Gibraltar Companies House, Registry of Companies, HM Government of Gibraltar
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Registration (Form CO-01) together with Memorandum and Articles of Association
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital; the company may issue a single ordinary share of GBP 1.00 subscribed at par without an escrow account requirement
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED: (1) That the company adopt the Memorandum and Articles of Association filed with the Gibraltar Registrar of Companies and confirm that the subscribers named in the incorporation application subscribe to 1 ordinary share of GBP 1.00 each at par, paid up in full. (2) That the registered office of the company be at [Registered Office Address], Gibraltar. (3) That [Director A] and [Director B] be appointed as first directors and that [Name] be appointed company secretary. (4) That the directors be authorized to open bank or EMI accounts, execute contracts, and file all necessary statutory returns. (5) Any one director may act alone.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Gibraltar Companies House, Registry of Companies (online via e-Registry)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a name reservation application through the Gibraltar Companies House e-Registry portal. Ensure the proposed corporate name contains 'Limited' or an approved abbreviation and is not misleading or identical to an existing registered name. Pay the reservation fee online.
required_dossiers: Certificate of incorporation of any foreign parent (if applicable)
Proof of authority to use the name (if reserved)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused, file a fresh application with an alternative name or lodge an appeal against the Registrar's decision within 21 days under the Companies Act 2014.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation and Execution of Constitutional Documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary Public / Authorized Legal Professional in Gibraltar
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the Memorandum and Articles of Association in English, incorporating standard limited liability and exempt-company provisions. Have each subscriber execute the memorandum before a notary public or an authorized witness. If the entity is a Bermuda Exempted Company classification, include the standard exempted-company objects clause and prohibit invitation to the public in Gibraltar.
required_dossiers: Consent of first director(s) and company secretary
Notarized identification documents of subscribers and first officers
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar queries any clause, amend the constitutional documents by supplemental memorandum and re-submit through the e-Registry within 14 days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upload the executed Form CO-01, Memorandum and Articles of Association, and required consents to the e-Registry. Pay the official filing fee of USD 250 (or GBP equivalent) by card or wire. The system issues an electronic acknowledgement immediately.
required_dossiers: Consent to act as company secretary
Registered office address confirmation from the service provider
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is rejected for formal defects, correct the deficiencies online within 7 days and re-upload. If rejected for substantive non-compliance, submit a new application with a full explanation and supporting documents.

step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon verification, the Registrar issues a Certificate of Incorporation electronically. The certificate confirms the company number, date of incorporation, and registered office. Download the certified copy and maintain it in the company's statutory records.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the certificate contains errors, request a formal correction by filing Form CO-14 with the Registrar and pay the rectification processing fee if required.

step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Where required under Part II of the Companies Act 2014, publish a notice of incorporation in the Gibraltar Gazette within 7 days of incorporation. File Form CO-02 confirming the registered office and Form CO-03 confirming the first directors and secretary. Keep an up-to-date register of members and directors at the registered office.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Gazette publication is delayed or rejected, file a corrective notice with the Gazette office and pay a late publication fee; the Registrar may accept a late filing if the company provides reasonable cause.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt - Category C (no physical development or discharge; minimal environmental footprint)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No industrial wastewater discharge; VOCs not applicable; compliance with WEEE Directive 2012/19/EU and RoHS Directive 2011/65/EU for any imported electronic hardware, and GDPR-aligned data storage practices in certified data centres.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety and electrical safety certification supplied by the licensed serviced-office provider; no structural load modifications; workplace health and safety clearance issued by the Gibraltar Safety at Work Inspectorate for the registered office premise.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Income Tax Office, H.M. Government of Gibraltar (Commissioner of Income Tax), e-filing through the Gibraltar Tax e-Services portal accessible via www.gibraltar.gov.gi; indirect tax on physical imports is administered by HM Customs Gibraltar (Asycuda World single window). HMRC of the United Kingdom is not the competent authority for Gibraltar, as Gibraltar is a self-governing British Overseas Territory with a distinct tax administration.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A Bermuda Exempted Company establishing a Gibraltar presence must: (1) apply for a Gibraltar Tax Reference Number (TRN) by filing the standard corporate registration questionnaire with the Income Tax Office, accompanied by certified copies of the Bermuda Certificate of Incorporation, Memorandum and Articles of Association, latest Certificate of Good Standing, and the Bermuda Exempted Undertakings Tax Protection Act 1966 Certificate of Exemption; (2) if a physical branch is opened, register as an 'overseas company' with the Gibraltar Registrar of Companies under the Companies Act 2014; (3) submit a board resolution evidencing the intended place of management and control, as this determines Gibraltar tax residence; (4) where staff are engaged, obtain an employer/Gibraltar Reference Number (GRN) with the Income Tax Office for Payroll (PAYE) compliance; and (5) when opening a Gibraltar bank account, present the TRN, registered-agent details, and the entity's structural diagram. No VAT registration ID is available because Gibraltar has no VAT/GST. Processing is ordinarily 5–10 business days; a Gibraltar tax representative is recommended.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Tax_Exempt_Zone — The Bermuda Exempted Company benefits from a statutory exemption under Bermuda law (no Bermuda income or capital tax until at least 2035). However, in Gibraltar, the operative rule is residence-based: a company incorporated in Gibraltar is resident there, while a foreign-incorporated company (including a Bermudian exempted company) becomes Gibraltar tax resident only if its management and control is exercised in Gibraltar. Once resident, it is subject to Gibraltar corporate income tax at 12.5% on worldwide profits, with credit for foreign taxes; if not managed and controlled in Gibraltar, it is non-resident and taxed only on Gibraltar-source income. The default pipeline posture is Tax_Exempt_Zone via Bermuda, but this status is fully preserved only if board meetings, strategic decisions, and operational control are exercised outside Gibraltar; otherwise, entity-level taxation in Gibraltar at 12.5% applies.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Gibraltar has no US-style 'check-the-box' election and no domestic hybrid-mismatch election. Available statutory elections under the Income Tax Act 2010 include: (a) group loss-relief and consortium surrender elections for Gibraltar-resident group members; (b) an election for qualifying trading companies to compute assessable profits on a deemed gross-margin basis where intra-group services are supplied at arm's length; (c) tonnage-tax election for qualifying shipping companies; and (d) gross-fee income assessment elections for regulated financial-services providers. Additionally, a non-resident company may evidence its status by formal board minute and organisational documentation confirming that management and control is exercised outside Gibraltar, which functions as the practical analogue to a 'check-the-box' foreign-entity election in tax-planning structures.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: No VAT or GST in Gibraltar. The only Gibraltar indirect tax is Import Duty levied under the Customs Ordinance on physical goods imported into Gibraltar at rates ranging from 0% to 130% by tariff heading, with most non-EU-origin consumer goods attracting 20% and EU/UK-origin goods generally at nil or preferential rates. Digital services, SaaS subscriptions, and intangible supplies are outside the scope of Gibraltar indirect tax. The UK's 20% VAT does not apply in Gibraltar and Gibraltar is not part of the UK VAT territory.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: Not applicable for VAT/GST (no such regime exists). A zero-threshold customs trader registration applies under the Customs Ordinance for any party importing goods into Gibraltar. For B2C digital supplies of SaaS to consumers, there is no Gibraltar indirect-tax registration or threshold; the merchant-of-record payment rails (Paddle and Lemon Squeezy) are the legal suppliers to end consumers and are responsible for collecting and remitting VAT/GST/digital services tax in the consumer's jurisdiction, including UK VAT and EU VAT via their own registrations.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Gibraltar imposes no real-time e-invoicing, fiscal clearance, digital stamping, or Continuous Transaction Control (CTC) mandate. There is no PEPPOL requirement and no government-authorised invoice repository for SaaS supplies. Commercial invoices issued via the merchant of record or by the Gibraltar entity are sufficient for record-keeping. The only electronic filing obligation with fiscal effect is the Asycuda World electronic customs declaration for physical import/export of goods.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Not applicable — Gibraltar has no VAT and therefore no zero-rating or refund mechanism for exports. SaaS and digital services exported from Gibraltar are 'outside the scope' of Gibraltar indirect tax rather than zero-rated. For physical goods, an outward export declaration suspends import duty and removes goods from the Gibraltar charge. Analytically, the platform-supplied B2B supply chain (Gibraltar entity selling to Paddle/Lemon Squeezy as merchant of record) falls under destination-country B2B place-of-supply rules, generally outside the Gibraltar entity's VAT return; any UK/EU VAT on consumer purchases is collected by the merchant of record, and the Gibraltar entity has no VAT refund entitlement to determine.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration / Single Administrative Document (physical goods only)
Bill of Lading, Air Waybill, or postal export evidence (physical goods only)
Commercial invoice and executed SaaS subscription agreement / terms of service
Merchant-of-record settlement statements from Paddle and Lemon Squeezy evidencing gross sales, platform fees, payment processing charges, and indirect taxes collected
Inward remittance records and bank statements demonstrating FX repatriation of net SaaS proceeds to the Gibraltar settlement account
Bermuda Certificate of Good Standing and Exemption Certificate, where applicable
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Because Gibraltar has no VAT, no fraudulent export zero-rating claim can be made; the substantive audit exposure is corporate tax residence. If the Income Tax Office determines that the Bermuda Exempted Company is managed and controlled in Gibraltar, it will retrospectively assess worldwide profits at 12.5% plus interest at 10% per annum and civil penalties up to 100% of the tax undercharged (up to 50% for negligence), with additional penalties for failure to file, and criminal prosecution for fraudulent evasion (unlimited fines and custodial sentences available on indictment in the Gibraltar Supreme Court). In parallel, the Bermuda Registrar of Companies may revoke exempted status for violation of the Exempted Undertakings Tax Protection Act 1966 conditions, retroactively lifting the Bermuda tax shield and exposing the entity to Bermuda payroll and land tax. The payment facilitators' merchant-of-record reports and settlement records are the primary evidence trail scrutinised in any residence audit.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of England (monetary authority for the sterling peg) and Gibraltar Financial Services Commission (GFSC) as the in-territory banking and conduct regulator; no separate Gibraltar central bank exists, and exchange control administration is subsumed within HM Treasury's pari passu application to Gibraltar.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Gibraltar has no standalone exchange control regime. The Gibraltar pound (GIP) is freely convertible at par to GBP, and both current-account flows (subscription fees, software royalties, intercompany service charges) and capital-account flows (intercompany loans, equity injections, dividend remittances) are unrestricted in law. Profit repatriation to the Bermuda exempted company requires only standard Gibraltarian Companies Act solvency declarations, board resolutions, and tax clearance evidence where distribution is linked to retained profits; no central bank approval or currency conversion permit is required. Practical frictions are limited to commercial correspondent-bank sanctions, AML controls, and proof-of-economic-substance expectations, not regulatory convertibility limits.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No mandatory surrender or conversion regime applies. Gibraltar imposes zero obligatory conversion ratios, no statutory repatriation timeline, and no surrender of export receipts. A consumer micro-SaaS business may retain proceeds in USD, EUR, GBP/GIP, or any freely tradable currency. The only relevant requirement is bank-level documentation that export receipts arise from genuine commercial activity, evidenced by SaaS subscription contracts, invoice schedules, and payment-aggregator settlement reports.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility: High for collection aggregation and low-value treasury; Medium as a primary banking layer. The target payment rails (Paddle, Lemon Squeezy) are principal collection intermediaries, making a fintech EMI suitable for temporary holding and quick FX conversion. Legal constraints: offshore digital EMIs such as Wise, Airwallex, Revolut Business, and similar are not Gibraltar-licensed banks under the Banking Act; they typically operate under UK or EEA e-money licences with permissive passported access to Gibraltar. In practice, a Bermuda exempted company can onboard to these EMIs remotely with strong UBO documentation, but many EMIs will flag the Bermuda domicile as an offshore tax-haven risk and impose lower thresholds or closure risk. Therefore the blueprint directs fintech EMIs to serve as inbound collection and settlement accelerators, while the primary treasury, capital escrow, and outbound disbursement-grade liquidity must remain in GFSC-regulated banks.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Tier-1 Gibraltar banks generally require at least one director or ultimate beneficial owner to attend a physical in-person interview before account activation. Fully remote opening is not available for offshore corporate structures; video-based interviews are allowed only in limited cases where a regulated introducer (Gibraltarian law firm, family-office adviser, or Big-4 accountant) provides an authenticated cover letter and existing banking sponsorship. The safest execution is a scheduled executive visit to the bank's Gibraltar premises, with due-diligence packs prepared in advance.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Bermuda exempted company is flagged as an offshore tax-haven entity with no local trading substance.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certificate of good standing from Bermuda Registry; certificate of incorporation; register of directors and shareholders; board resolution appointing Gibraltar managers; Gibraltar lease; employment contracts and social-security filings; annual accounts; narrative substance memorandum describing the Bermuda holding role and Gibraltar operating role.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Ultimate beneficial owner (UBO) chain appears nontransparent due to intermediate Bermuda parent or nominee shareholders.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Full beneficial-ownership chart naming every natural person; certified passport copies; proof of address; negative press and PEP/legal-action screening report; statutory beneficial ownership declaration; company secretarial letter; evidence of the true economic rationale for the Bermuda holding layer.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-frequency consumer SaaS subscription receipts from many low-value card transactions appear as heavy, unrelated retail turnover.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Paddle and Lemon Squeezy merchant statements; payment-aggregator agreements; sample end-customer subscription invoices; product and pricing pages; transaction-volume reconciliation model; chargeback and refund policy documentation; API-based sales reporting export.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Economic-substance mismatch between the Bermuda exempted company and the Gibraltar operating entity raises concern of letterbox operation.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Intercompany services and licensing agreement; transfer-pricing documentation using CUP or transactional margin method; payroll records for Gibraltar employees; board meeting minutes held in Gibraltar; IP ownership and sub-licence registry; Gibraltar VAT registration evidence (if applicable); policies for data protection and SaaS service delivery.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound capital from the Bermuda exempted company to the Gibraltar operating account should be routed by SWIFT MT103 or MT202 over correspondent banking. The recommended ISO 20022 category purpose code is 'CAPH' for capital injection or intercompany investment; when the injection is structured as a shareholder loan, the bank may require purpose code 'B230' or 'LOAN' with a signed loan agreement. The following compliance packet must accompany the transfer: board resolution from Bermuda shareholders authorising the funds flow; notarised certificate of incumbency; source-of-funds statement referencing the Bermuda audited balance sheet; intercompany loan agreement (if debt) or equity subscription instrument; signed beneficiary attestation. No mandatory Gibraltar exchange-control filing applies, but the receiving bank's currency conversion desk should be pre-notified to avoid automatic inspection on a potentially matching name-screening hit.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For outbound vendor, infrastructure, and licensing settlements, the clearing rails are: (a) SWIFT MT103 for global non-SEPA USD/EUR/GBP payments, with settled delivery via Fedwire/CHIPS/CHAPS; (b) SEPA Credit Transfer (SEPA CT) for EU/UK-region EUR payments, executed through UK or Gibraltar correspondent banks participating in SEPA; (c) Commercial Irrevocable Documentary Credit (LC) only for high-value supply contracts requiring documentary compliance and trade finance; (d) virtual corporate cards linked to the primary account for recurring low-value SaaS infrastructure and platform fees. Documentary disbursement mandates should include an invoice, purchase order, acceptance of service, and, where relevant, beneficial-ownership declaration of the recipient. Multi-party settlement through Paddle/Lemon Squeezy is treated as an inward clearing rail before funds enter the treasury ledger.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: FX forward contracts (deliverable, up to 12-month tenors)
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) on GIP/GBP pegged pairs only where approved by bank treasury policy
Vanilla FX options (put/call for revenue conversion risk mitigation)
Currency basis swaps for intercompany debt servicing

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Bermuda Exempted Company Annual Return and Government Fee (base band for authorized capital ≤ BMD 12,000)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually by 31 July for the preceding year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing incurs penalty of BMD 100–BMD 500; three consecutive years of non-filing triggers administrative strike-off and dissolution under Companies Act 1981 s.279; directors may be disqualified.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Bermuda Beneficial Ownership Register (BORA) Annual Confirmation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Bermuda Registry of Beneficial Ownership / Financial Intelligence Agency
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually by 31 July, and within 30 days of any share transfer or change of beneficial ownership
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-compliance attracts monetary penalty up to BMD 20,000; continued default may result in strike-off and imprisonment of responsible officers for up to 6 months.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Bermuda Economic Substance Declaration (ESD) or Nil Return
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Bermuda Registrar of Companies / International Tax Authority
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually by 31 July for the accounting period ended in the preceding year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fixed penalty of BMD 5,000 for first default, BMD 10,000 for subsequent defaults; persistent failure may lead to strike-off and exchange of information with UK/EU authorities.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Gibraltar Annual Return / Confirmation Statement of Foreign Company
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 42 days of the annual return date, being the anniversary of the Gibraltar branch registration date
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of £100 per day, capped at £1,000; default continuing for six months may result in cancellation of the branch registration and administrative strike-off.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Independent audit is mandatory if the Bermuda exempted company has a shareholder resident in Bermuda, carries on business through an actual place of business in Bermuda, holds a Bermuda Monetary Authority licence, or solicits public investment. Under Section 87B, a non-resident company with no Bermuda-resident shareholders and fewer than 51 members may dispense with audit; a micro SaaS with gross assets below BMD 1,000,000 and gross annual revenue below BMD 3,000,000 may adopt unaudited status by written member resolution.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Bermuda permits IFRS as issued by the IASB or US GAAP for statutory financial statements; if branch accounts are filed in Gibraltar, the financial statements must be prepared in accordance with IFRS as adopted by the EU and reconciled to the Bermuda accounts, giving a true and fair view under the Companies Act 1981 (Bermuda).

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The Bermuda Annual Return must be accompanied by confirmation that the Beneficial Ownership Register on the BORA platform is up to date. Any share transfer or change of beneficial ownership must be filed within 30 days. Annually by 31 July, the company must re-confirm the list of beneficial owners, approve or amend the register, and certify that all prior-year share transfers are reflected in the Register of Members.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 1,500 – USD 3,500 per annum, covering Bermuda registered office and resident agent plus Gibraltar branch agent
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 3,000 – USD 8,000 per audit cycle if audit exemption is not available or is voluntarily adopted

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 12.5% standard Gibraltar Corporation Tax; 10% preferential band applies to the first GIP 256,000 of chargeable profit of a qualifying small company; 0% Bermuda corporate tax if the exempted company holds a Tax Exemption Certificate and is not managed and controlled in Gibraltar
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Qualifying small/micro companies with assessable profits and payroll not exceeding statutory thresholds (approximately GIP 256,000 per annum) pay 10% on the first tranche of chargeable profit. Full deduction for ordinary SaaS operating expenditure, platform processing fees, and revenue software development costs. Statutory capital allowances available for qualifying computer hardware and software. No Gibraltar IP-Box or patent-box.
